text:
natalie: Heads up — planning to roll the namespace-affinity policy (project->workspace mapping) to canary tomorrow morning. Quick question: does org-level KMS binding implicitly grant decrypt to service principals created in sibling workspaces? I'm fuzzy on the resolver logic.

jon: short answer: it shouldn't. KMS assertion currently includes workspace_id in the principal. But we shipped a canonicalization tweak last month that might collapse empty workspace tags.

maya: @jon can you point to the exact resolver code? worried about org-level keys backing customer buckets.

jon: snippet from authz resolver: 
```
principal := fmt.Sprintf("org:%s:workspace:%s:sa:%s", orgID, workspaceID, saName)
if workspaceID == "" {
  // legacy fallback: use org-only principal
  principal = fmt.Sprintf("org:%s:sa:%s", orgID, saName)
}
bindingKey := fmt.Sprintf("org/%s/kms/%s", orgID, keyID)
```
The bug is the `workspaceID == ""` fallback — if a SA is missing workspace metadata we return org-scoped principal.

liam: that matches the regression we saw in the friday canary — bootstrap created SAs without the workspace annotation. They ended up with org-scoped principals and could decrypt.

natalie: two immediate concerns: 1) rolling this policy could expose cross-workspace decrypts 2) audit logs need clear workspace attribution for kms_decrypt events. Quick mitigations?

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for namespace-affinity-policy:v2 in us-west-2 :rocket:

maya: mitigation options: 
- quick block: add explicit deny when workspaceID is missing
- patch bootstrap to always set workspace annotation on SA creation
- tighten KMS authorizer to require exact principal match and emit audit event on mismatch

jon: I can add the authorizer strict-match + metric. PR will also emit a debug audit event when a fallback happened.

liam: ops can pause the rollout while we patch. Also recommend running an audit query for kms_decrypt where workspace_id is null to see scope.

natalie: @sophia can you run the audit query and surface any recent decrypts with missing workspace_id?

sophia: running now. Example ES query I used: 
```
GET /logs/_search
{ "query": { "bool": { "must": [ {"term":{"event":"kms_decrypt"}}, {"bool": {"must_not": {"exists": {"field": "workspace_id"}}}} ] } } }
```

sophia: found 6 decrypts in the past 7 days with workspace_id missing. Short IDs: kdt-43, kdt-77, kdt-102, kdt-119, kdt-143, kdt-188.

natalie: OK. Action items: jon = add hard check in authorizer (reject if workspace empty unless explicit org-binding exists and log it), maya = patch bootstrap to set workspace annotation, liam = coordinate pause + rollback knob for canary, sophia = collect full audit entries and timeline. I'll open a short customer-facing runbook in the incident queue; CISO should be cc'd if anything shows cross-tenant decrypt.

jon: opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/authz/pull/509 — adds strict-match and metric `kms_assertion_mismatch_total`. Also adds an audit event with reason `fallback_org_principal`.

maya: bootstrap patch submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bootstrap/pull/123 — ensures `redwood.workplace_id` annotation is always set at SA creation.

liam: pausing canary in us-west-2 now. Will hold global rollout until we get green from sec and ops. :white_check_mark:

sophia: exported audit CSV to /mnt/sec/audit/1739500000-kms-null-workspace.csv and uploaded to the secure bucket. I included full request_ids and timestamps.

sec-bot: Created ticket SEC-321: potential cross-workspace KMS access due to missing workspace annotation. Priority: P2.

natalie: thanks all. We'll run end-to-end test (authz + bootstrap + audit replay) before resuming. Ping this thread with any new decrypts or auth failures. :eyes:
